title: Ranbir Kapoor and Yash Are Taking Ramayana to Comic-Con. No Indian Film Has Ever Done This.
excerpt: The most expensive Indian film ever made gets a full panel at San Diego Comic-Con on July 23, with the worldwide trailer dropping July 24. Hans Zimmer and AR Rahman are scoring it. This is not normal.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Ranbir Kapoor and Yash will present Ramayana at San Diego Comic-Con on July 23.
  • Ramayana is the most expensive Indian film ever, budgeted over ₹600 crore.
  • The film features a star-studded cast including Ranbir Kapoor, Yash, and A.R. Rahman.
  • The trailer drops on July 24, aiming to correct mixed reactions from the first teaser.
  • Ramayana: Part One is set for a Diwali 2026 release, competing with major Hollywood films.

Something that has never happened before in Indian cinema is about to happen in San Diego.

On July 23, Ranbir Kapoor and Yash will walk onto a stage at the San Diego Comic-Con — the largest pop culture convention on the planet — and present a full panel for Ramayana, Nitesh Tiwari's two-part epic that is already the most expensive Indian film ever produced. The next day, July 24, the official trailer drops worldwide.

Let that sink in. An Indian film. At Comic-Con. With its lead actors. In the same hall where Marvel reveals its Phase plans and *The Lord of the Rings* got its standing ovation.

This isn't just marketing. This is a declaration.

The Panel

The SDCC listing confirms the panel for July 23 at 3:15 PM PDT, featuring producer Namit Malhotra, director Nitesh Tiwari, and stars Ranbir Kapoor and Yash. The event promises exclusive first-look footage, live performances, and what the organisers are calling "an unforgettable experience."

> "From Bharat to the world. For thousands of years, the Ramayana has inspired generations through its timeless ideals of dharma, maryada, courage, and compassion. Now, it begins a new journey."

> "For a project reportedly budgeted at over ₹600 crore across both parts, "looks unfinished" is not feedback you can afford."

That was the makers' official announcement, posted Saturday. Understated it is not.

The Cast and the Scale

The ensemble is staggering. Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama. Sai Pallavi as Sita. Yash — the man who made *KGF* a cultural phenomenon — as Ravana. Sunny Deol as Hanuman. Ravi Dubey as Lakshman. Rakul Preet Singh as Surpanakha. Kunal Kapoor as Lord Indra. And rounding out the supporting cast: Lara Dutta, Arun Govil (the original Ram from the 1987 television *Ramayan*), and Sheeba Chadha.

![San Diego — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/e/ea/La_Jolla_Shores_view_%28cropped%29.jpg)

Behind the camera, the firepower is equally absurd. Nitesh Tiwari — the man behind *Dangal*, the highest-grossing Indian film of all time — is directing. The music is being composed by A.R. Rahman and Hans Zimmer together, which is a sentence that should not exist but somehow does. The visual effects come from DNEG, Namit Malhotra's own VFX house, which has won eight Academy Awards for its work on films like *Inception*, *Interstellar*, and *Tenet*.

Why the Trailer Matters More Than Usual

Here's the part that makes the July 24 trailer drop genuinely high-stakes: the first teaser did not land cleanly.

The "Rama glimpse" that was released earlier drew mixed reactions. Some were moved by the scale and ambition. Others felt the visual effects looked unfinished — a criticism that stung, given that the film's entire identity rests on delivering visuals that match or exceed what Hollywood produces. For a project reportedly budgeted at over ₹600 crore across both parts, "looks unfinished" is not feedback you can afford.

The Comic-Con trailer is the correction. It's the version that has to prove the VFX has been polished, the emotional beats land, and the film justifies its gargantuan ambition. If it works, Ramayana becomes the most anticipated release in Indian cinema history. If it doesn't, the conversation shifts from "when do I book tickets?" to "should I wait for reviews?"

The Diwali Battlefield

Ramayana: Part One is locked in for a Diwali 2026 release. It's going head-to-head with the Hollywood monster franchise entry that just dropped its own teaser — setting up what might be the biggest box office clash in Indian history.

The second part is planned for Diwali 2027, making this a two-year commitment from the makers that will define whether Indian mythological cinema can genuinely compete on the global stage.

Why NRIs Should Pay Attention

This is the part that matters most for the diaspora. Ramayana is releasing globally in IMAX, which means NRI audiences in the US, UK, Canada, Australia, and the Gulf will have premium-format access from Day 1.

But more than that — for the first time, an Indian film is treating Comic-Con as its launchpad. Not a Bollywood award show. Not a press conference in Mumbai. San Diego. That's a signal to the global entertainment industry that Indian cinema is no longer content with being a regional market. It wants the same stage as Marvel, DC, and the Tolkien estate.

For desi fans in the US, this is your moment. If you're anywhere near San Diego on July 23, you might witness something historic: Ranbir Kapoor and Yash introducing Rama and Ravana to the same crowd that gave standing ovations to Robert Downey Jr.'s Iron Man reveal.

The trailer drops July 24. Mark it.
